summary: Mainz's central garages are run mostly by the municipal PMG Parken in Mainz GmbH (about 10,000 spaces in roughly 25 to 28 facilities, owned by the Mainzer Aufbaugesellschaft and the city), not by the transport company. Typical city-centre garage tariffs are 0.80 euro for the first half hour and a 10.00 euro daytime maximum (15.50 euro at Römisches Theater and CineStar), with a cheap night subscription, Park@Night, since July 2025 at 16.99 euro per month; the city has a live free/occupied guidance system fed by PMG occupancy data, and PMG added 26 charging points at Parkhaus Rathaus in February 2026. On the street, resident permit fees rose on 1 July 2025 from 30 euro to roughly 130-300 euro per year, free parking for electric cars ended in 2024, and the Große Bleiche was closed to private cars on 1 August 2026 after the Binger Straße tram link opened on 10 August 2026; the inner-city tram route was decided in April 2025 with opening expected 2032-2034. Regional press and an IHK survey report that building sites and traffic changes hurt city-centre access, while park-and-ride in Mainz has remained minor (a 2019 study saw demand for only about 70 to 110 spaces at the Hechtsheim end of the tram). Mainz is a commuter city, with roughly 80,000 in-commuters.

items.text: The municipal PMG Parken in Mainz GmbH (owned by the Mainzer Aufbaugesellschaft and the city) runs most central garages; its company page (read 21 October 2026) gives about 10,000 spaces in 25 facilities, eight owned and the rest leased or managed, plus about 2,300 spaces on the Universitätsmedizin grounds. PMG's other pages give 27 or 28 facilities, so the count is approximate, and the parking ticket also serves as a bus and tram ticket of Mainzer Mobilität.

PMG's FAQ (read 21 October 2026) says Mainz has a city parking guidance system and that garage occupancy figures are sent regularly to the city, so the free/occupied display is based on live data; a garage shown as 'occupied' may still have spaces reserved for permanent parkers. Payment is cashless everywhere except Parkhaus Rheinallee III, and a lost ticket costs 25 euro.

PMG moved its garages to licence plate recognition: the first six were converted in 2024 (PMG 40-year page), and Parkhaus CityPort at Hauptbahnhof West was closed fully from 12 May to 1 June 2025 for the same change (city statement quoted by Mainz&).
items.source_title: Mainz& - Baustelle am Hauptbahnhof Mainz, Parkhaus CityPort dicht

items.text: Typical PMG city-centre tariff (Parkhaus Kronberger Hof, Löhrstraße, Rathaus, Deutschhausplatz and others, page read 21 October 2026): 0.80 euro first half hour, 1.00 euro second and third half hour, 1.10 euro fourth, then 2.10 euro per hour; daytime (6:00-19:00) maximum 10.00 euro, night rate (19:00-6:00) 0.90 euro per half hour with a 5.00 euro night maximum.

Some PMG garages price differently (pages read 21 October 2026): Römisches Theater and CineStar have a daytime maximum of 15.50 euro, Gonsberg Campus gives the first hour free then 1.00 euro (second hour) and 1.50 euro per hour with an 8.00 euro maximum, and Tiefgarage Weinlager charges 1.00 euro per hour and 24.00 euro per 24 hours. Parkhaus Wallstraße (303 spaces, outside the inner city) charges 3.00 euro per 24 hours with a 6.00 euro weekend flat rate (Saturday 8:00 to Monday 8:00).
items.source_title: PMG Parkhaus CineStar / Gonsberg Campus / Weinlager - Tarife

items.text: PMG special tariffs listed in its FAQ (read 21 October 2026): a 5 euro event tariff in Kronberger Hof, Theater and Parkplatz Schloss (Mon-Sat 18:00-8:00, Sun 10:00-16:00), a 4 euro cinema tariff at CineStar, 20 percent off for Taubertsbergbad swimming pool visitors, and 10 percent off short-term parking with Park&Go.

On 31 March 2025 PMG, with Lord Mayor Nino Haase and transport councillor Janina Steinkrüger, announced the night tariff 'Park@Night' from 1 July 2025: 16.99 euro per month for Mon-Sat 17:00-9:00 and all day Sundays/holidays, or 26.99 euro with all of Saturday. PMG said about 5,000 spaces were available at night in the participating garages, and the city planned to evaluate the offer after three months.

Park@Night is now offered as a one-year contract at 16.99 euro (Park@Night) or 26.99 euro (Park@Night Plus) per month, valid in 18 listed garages (Bleiche, Augustusplatz, CineStar, CityPort, Deutschhausplatz, Gonsberg Campus, Kronberger Hof, Löhrstraße, Rathaus, Rheinufer, Römisches Theater, Schillerplatz, Schloss, Taubertsberg, Theater, Wallstraße, Weinlager, Weißliliengasse); the PMG offers page was read on 21 October 2026. It requires a prior Park&Go registration (plate recognition or card), and Park&Go gives 10 percent off short-term tariffs.

PMG capacities listed on its site (read 21 October 2026) include CityPort 1,105, Taubertsberg 767, Rheinufer 497, Rathaus 545, Kronberger Hof 460, Weißliliengasse 460, CineStar 459, Römisches Theater 436, Schillerplatz 420, Gonsberg Campus 316, Wallstraße 303, Bleiche 227, Theater 207, Deutschhausplatz 190, Weinlager 171, Löhrstraße 145 and Rheinallee III 94 spaces. These are PMG's stated total spaces and can differ from the subset of spaces covered by a live feed.
items.source_title: PMG Parken in Mainz - Parkhäuser / Tarife

items.text: At the launch of Park@Night in March 2025 the Lord Mayor said the PMG garages, about 10,000 spaces, were only about 10 percent occupied at night. PMG's director said its earlier night rate of 50 to 80 euro per month and permanent bays at 150 to 179 euro per month had not been well accepted.
items.source_title: Mainz& - Neuer Tarif Park@Night ab Juli in Mainz

items.text: On 27 February 2026 PMG put 26 new charging points into service in Parkhaus Rathaus (24 on level 2, 2 accessible on level 1), described as the first accessible public charging points in Mainz. Power comes largely from the PV system on the Rheingoldhalle roof, the price is a flat 54 cent per kWh including VAT, and further charging points were announced for Parkhaus Löhrstraße in 2026.
items.source_title: PMG - Neue E-Ladestationen im Parkhaus Rathaus

items.text: Mainz raised resident parking permit fees on 1 July 2025 from 30 euro per year (60 euro for a two-year permit) to a size-based formula (31.20 euro times vehicle length times width), giving roughly 130 to 300 euro per year; new permits are valid for one year and there is no social discount. The city counted about 14,500 permits against roughly 8,900 public spaces in about 25 resident zones, with 7,600 permits in the Neustadt (regional press report).
items.source_title: Mainz& - Anwohnerparken in Mainz wird drastisch teurer

items.text: Mainz ended free on-street parking for electric cars in September 2024; the 2017 exemption had been extended once in 2022, and e-vehicles now need a parking ticket except at charging stations. The city said about 10 percent of Mainz-registered cars were electric or hybrid.
items.source_title: Mainz& - Kein kostenloses Parken mehr für E-Autos in Mainz

items.text: On 1 August 2026 the city closed Große Bleiche between Flachsmarkt and Peter-Altmeier-Allee to private cars (buses, taxis and bikes only) as a 'Modalfilter' decided by the council in June 2026 to protect the new Binger Straße tram link; the transport department expects about 80 percent less traffic there. A regional newspaper reported confusion and detours via Bauhofstraße.
items.source_title: Mainz& - Sperrung Große Bleiche in Mainz Richtung Rhein

items.text: The new tram line through Binger Straße (Alicenplatz to Münsterplatz) went into service on 10 August 2026; line 53 from Lerchenberg now runs from Hauptbahnhof West through Binger Straße to the new stop Münsterplatz D. Construction ran from June 2024 to August 2026, and the street now has wider footways and cycle paths.
items.source_title: M wie Zukunft - Teilprojekt 1 Binger Straße

items.text: The Mainz city council decided on 9 April 2025 on the preferred route for the inner-city tram: Ludwigstraße - Flachsmarkt - Große Bleiche - Rheinallee - Goethe- and Nahestraße - Zollhafen. The published timeline foresees planning approval proceedings from late 2027, a construction decision in early 2029 and opening between 2032 and 2034.
items.source_title: M wie Zukunft - Teilprojekt Innenstadt, Planungsstand

items.text: An IHK Rheinhessen survey in August 2026 found 78 percent of responding firms rated the economic effect of Mainz's traffic situation as mostly negative, and 94 percent called the car important for reaching the city centre; four in five said access to their site had worsened since 2024. Federal commuter data cited in the article give about 80,000 in-commuters (62.4 percent of roughly 128,000 jobs) in June 2025.
items.source_title: Mainz& - Wirtschaft kritisiert Verkehrspolitik in Mainz

items.text: In 2019 a city-commissioned study saw demand for only about 70 to 110 park-and-ride spaces at the Hechtsheim end of the tram; the city then negotiated for up to 200 commuter spaces in the old garage at the Kurmainz-Kaserne and said the only existing P+R lot was at the Hechtsheim tram terminus. This is a 2019 plan and a dated article, not current capacity.
items.source_title: Mainz& - Park & Ride in Parkhaus an Kurmainz-Kaserne?

gaps: https://www.mainz.de/ (all pages, including parken, Bewohnerparken, park-ride, Stadtrat/Ratsinformation and the PDF mainz.de/medien/internet/downloads/RP_Noerdliche-Neustadt_parkraumkonzept.pdf) returned HTTP 503 Service Unavailable on 21 October 2026, so no official city pages could be read; resident-parking and Modalfilter facts rest on regional press (Mainz&) only.

Mobilithek (https://mobilithek.info/) is a JavaScript application whose offer pages could not be read as text, so the Mainz parking guidance data offer and its description could not be verified; the live guidance system is documented only through PMG's FAQ.
No Park@Night evaluation, subscriber numbers or utilisation figures were found; the city said in March 2025 it would evaluate after three months.

No current official list of park-and-ride sites and capacities (Hechtsheim/Mühldreieck, Layenhof, Lerchenberg, Kurmainz-Kaserne) was found; only 2019 press reports, so current P+R capacity is unknown.
The Allgemeine Zeitung and SWR could not be searched or opened (not accessible to the search tool), so regional press coverage relies on the independent online paper Mainz& (opinionated in places).

Not found: the council papers (Ratsinformationssystem) for the 2025 resident-parking fee ordinance and the June 2026 Modalfilter resolution, Quartiersgarage decisions, Umweltspur or pedestrian-zone decisions, and any Mainz garage tariff council decision (PMG sets its own tariffs; no tariff change date was found).

Our feed shows capacities such as Römisches Theater 247, Kupferberg 515, Kronberger Hof 215, Trajanstraße 225, Löhrstraße 71, while PMG lists Römisches Theater 436, Kronberger Hof 460 and Löhrstraße 145; Kupferberg and Trajanstraße are not on PMG's list, so their operators were not identified.

Dropped for the 18-item cap (all sourced): Heiligkreuz tram decision of 19 June 2026, 0-Euro-Samstag (free buses on first Saturday of the month), Mainz 05 match-day park-and-ride at the Messegelände, 2020 diesel-ban settlement, 2025 green-verge enforcement dispute, and the 2022 PMG presentation.
